arxiv-1807-03812.title: Demonstrating the Principles of Aperture Synthesis with Table-Top Laboratory Exercises
arxiv-1807-03812.creator: \firstname J. M. \lastname Marr \fnsep, \firstname A. E. E. \lastname Rogers, \firstname V. L. \lastname Fish, \firstname F. P. \lastname Wilkin, \firstname M. B. \lastname Arndt, \firstname G. \lastname Holodak, \firstname K. \lastname Durkota
arxiv-1807-03812.description: Abstract Many undergraduate radio astronomy courses are unable to give a detailed treatment of aperture synthesis due to time constraints and limited math backgrounds of students. We have taken a laboratory-based approach to teaching radio interferometry using a set of college-level, table-top exercises.

arxiv-2104-03392.title: Edsger W. Dijkstra: a Commemoration
arxiv-2104-03392.creator: Krzysztof R. Apt, Tony Hoare[2mm] (editors)
arxiv-2104-03392.description: Abstract This article is a multiauthored portrait of Edsger Wybe Dijkstra that consists of testimonials written by several friends, colleagues, and students of his. It provides unique insights into his personality, working style and habits, and his influence on other computer scientists, as a researcher, teacher, and mentor.

arxiv-2104-04704.title: DuRIN: A Deep-unfolded Sparse Seismic Reflectivity Inversion Network
arxiv-2104-04704.creator: Swapnil Mache, Praveen Kumar Pokala, Kusala Rajendran, and Chandra Sekhar Seelamantula
arxiv-2104-04704.description: Abstract We consider the reflection seismology problem of recovering the locations of interfaces and the amplitudes of reflection coefficients from seismic data, which are vital for estimating the subsurface structure. The reflectivity inversion problem is typically solved using greedy algorithms and iterative techniques.

arxiv-2106-09349.title: Blockchain Oracle Design Patterns
arxiv-2106-09349.creator: Amirmohammad Pasdar 1,2 , Zhongli Dong 1,3 , Young Choon Lee 2
arxiv-2106-09349.description: Abstract Blockchain is a form of distributed ledger technology (DLT) where data is shared among users connected over the internet. Transactions are data state changes on the blockchain that are permanently recorded in a secure and transparent way without the need of a third party.

arxiv-2211-16038.title: Data-efficient Modeling of Optical Matrix Multipliers Using Transfer Learning
arxiv-2211-16038.description: Abstract We demonstrate transfer learning-assisted neural network models for optical matrix multipliers with scarce measurement data. Our approach uses < 10 % <10\% of experimental data needed for best performance and outperforms analytical models for a Mach-Zehnder interferometer mesh. A. Cem 1,* , O. Jovanovic 1 , S. Yan 2 , Y. arxiv-2310-11736.title: Layered Models can "Automatically" Regularize and Discover Low-Dimensional Structures via Feature Learning
arxiv-2310-11736.creator: Yunlu Chen, Yang Li, Keli Liu, Feng Ruan
arxiv-2310-11736.description: Abstract Layered models like neural networks appear to extract key features from data through empirical risk minimization, yet the theoretical understanding for this process remains unclear. Motivated by these observations, we study a two-layer nonparametric regression model where the input undergoes a linear transformation followed by a nonlinear mapping to predict the output, mirroring the structure of two-layer neural networks.

arxiv-2405-05053.title: Observation of an unconventional giant negative exchange bias effect in La 0.5 Sr 0.5 Co 0.85 Nb 0.15 O 3
arxiv-2405-05053.creator: Rishabh Shukla, B. Schwarz, R. S. Dhaka
arxiv-2405-05053.description: Abstract We find an unconventional giant negative exchange bias (EB) of H EB H_{\rm EB} = –14.1 kOe at 2 K (cooling field of 50 kOe) in the cluster spin-glass (CSG) La 0.5 Sr 0.5 Co 0.85 Nb 0.15 O 3 perovsikte cobaltites.

arxiv-2406-11073.title: Exploring the Limitations of Detecting Machine-Generated Text
arxiv-2406-11073.creator: Jad Doughman, Osama Mohammed Afzal, Hawau Olamide Toyin, Shady Shehata, Preslav Nakov, Zeerak Talat
arxiv-2406-11073.description: Abstract Recent improvements in the quality of the generations by large language models have spurred research into identifying machine-generated text. Such work often presents high-performing detectors. However, humans and machines can produce text in different styles and domains, yet the the performance impact of such on machine generated text detection systems remains unclear.

arxiv-2408-08059.title: Maximally Permissive Reward Machines
arxiv-2408-08059.creator: Giovanni Varricchione, Natasha Alechina, Mehdi Dastani, Brian Logan
arxiv-2408-08059.description: Abstract Reward machines allow the definition of rewards for temporally extended tasks and behaviors. Specifying “informative” reward machines can be challenging. One way to address this is to generate reward machines from a high-level abstract description of the learning environment, using techniques such as AI planning.

arxiv-2409-14925.title: DanceCamAnimator: Keyframe-Based Controllable 3D Dance Camera Synthesis
arxiv-2409-14925.creator: Zixuan Wang, Jiayi Li, Xiaoyu Qin, Shikun Sun, Songtao Zhou, Jia Jia, Jiebo Luo
arxiv-2409-14925.description: Abstract . Synthesizing camera movements from music and dance is highly challenging due to the contradicting requirements and complexities of dance cinematography. Unlike human movements, which are always continuous, dance camera movements involve both continuous sequences of variable lengths and sudden drastic changes to simulate the switching of multiple cameras.

arxiv-2501-17891.title: Statistical Tools for Frequency Response Functions from Posture Control Experiments: Estimation of Probability of a Sample and Comparison Between Groups of Unpaired Samples
arxiv-2501-17891.creator: Vittorio Lippi \orcidID 0000-0001-5520-8974
arxiv-2501-17891.description: Abstract The frequency response function (FRF) is an established way to describe the outcome of experiments in posture control literature. The FRF is an empirical transfer function between an input stimulus and the induced body segment sway profile, represented as a vector of complex values associated with a vector of frequencies.

arxiv-2505-07951.title: Cosmological scalar perturbations for a metric reconstructed from group field theory
arxiv-2505-07951.creator: Steffen Gielen, Lisa Mickel
arxiv-2505-07951.description: Abstract While homogeneous cosmologies have long been studied in the group field theory (GFT) approach to quantum gravity, including a quantum description of cosmological perturbations is highly non-trivial. Here we apply a recent proposal for reconstructing an effective spacetime metric in GFT to the case of a metric with small inhomogeneities over a homogeneous background.

Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary shall take, compile, and publish censuses of manufactures, of mineral industries, and of other businesses, including the distributive trades, service establishments, and transportation (exclusive of means of transportation for which statistics are required by law to be filed.
